message.content:
# Meeting Briefing: Hugging Face
**Date:** November 20, 2026  
**Time:** 10:00 AM (+05:30)  

## Recent developments
* **Nvidia Acquisition & Regulatory Inquiry:** Following Hugging Face’s landmark $12.9 billion deal to join Nvidia, the U.S. Department of Justice initiated inquiries regarding its potential impact on market competition and Nvidia's control over open-source AI model distribution channels [1, 2, 3]. CEO Clément Delangue has publicly vowed to continue fighting for open-source AI following the transition [2].
* **Security & Open-Source Pressures:** Chief Policy Officer Irene Solaiman warned on TechCrunch’s *Equity* podcast that a rising wave of cyberattacks targeting open-source infrastructure risks pushing the industry toward tighter access controls, potentially threatening platform openness [1].
* **Cybersecurity Incident Response:** CEO Clément Delangue disclosed at the Miami AI Summit that when Hugging Face faced an autonomous AI agent cyberattack, proprietary API guardrails failed to assist defenders. Instead, the platform successfully neutralized the threat by relying on an open-source model (GLM 5.3 developed in China) running on Nvidia infrastructure [3]. Concurrently, the platform has faced scrutiny over hosting models capable of offensive cyber use, resulting in the removal of specific "abliterated" models [5].

## Talking points
* **The Nvidia Integration & Market Position:** Discuss how the Nvidia partnership impacts enterprise distribution channels, developer autonomy, and open-source platform neutrality amid DOJ antitrust scrutiny [2, 3].
* **Balancing Openness and Security:** Address the tension highlighted by executive leadership regarding cyberattacks and malicious actors hosting "abliterated" offensive models versus maintaining unhindered open-source accessibility [1, 5].
* **Enterprise AI Adoption:** Build on CEO Clément Delangue’s Miami AI Summit thesis that every company is becoming an AI builder [3], focusing on how to steer enterprises away from heavy reliance on closed-source APIs (such as OpenAI and Anthropic) [3].

## Open questions
* How will the structural integration with Nvidia alter Hugging Face's operational independence and commitment to platform neutrality under ongoing DOJ inquiries?
* What specific policy and technical frameworks is Hugging Face deploying to mitigate the rise of automated cyberattacks and malicious "abliterated" models without compromising the core open-source ethos?
* How does Hugging Face plan to reassure enterprise clients concerned about supply chain security and compliance given recent high-profile platform threats?

## Sources
* [1] [Open-Source AI Cybersecurity: 5 Hugging Face Risks [2026]](https://shattered.io/hugging-face-solaiman-open-source-ai-cyberattacks-two-attacks-2026)
* [2] [Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open-source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/hugging-face-ceo-vows-to-keep-fighting-for-open-source-ai-after-jensen-huangs-exit)
* [3] [At Miami AI Summit, Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue predicts every company will become an AI builder - Refresh Miami](https://refreshmiami.com/news/at-miami-ai-summit-hugging-face-ceo-clem-delangue-predicts-every-company-will-necome-an-ai-builder)
* [5] [Hugging Face appears to be hosting a load of models that could be used for cyber attacks](https://www.transformernews.ai/p/hugging-face-appears-to-be-hosting)
